# Adjudication Task — Chapter 608

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃608화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|나는 눈앞의 중년인을 빤히 바라보았다.
  6|
  7|도널드 도람프 주니어.
  8|
  9|수조 원의 재산과 그룹을 소유한 재벌이자, 과거 미 대통령이었던 아버지에 이어 미합중국 역사상 역대 세 번째 부자(父子) 대통령이라는 기록을 세운 인물이다.
 10|
 11|마치 영국 신사처럼 멀끔한 인상의 그는 실제 나이에 비해 20년은 젊어 보였고, 우리를 향한 웃음에는 진심이 담겨 있었다.
 12|
 13|「어서 오십시오, 두 분 모두.」
 14|
 15|우리는 아버지와는 다르게 머리를 깔끔하게 빗어넘긴 도람프 대통령과 악수를 나누었다.
 16|
 17|TV나 인터넷 기사를 통해서만 보던 미국 대통령을 이렇게 만나게 될 줄이야. 실물을 보면서도 신기한 마음이다.
 18|
 19|「하하, 그런 눈으로 보실 것 없습니다. 오히려 저야말로 신기하니까요. 말로만 듣던 두 분을 오늘에서야 뵙게 되는군요.」
 20|
 21|최 팀장이 유창한 발음으로 대답했다.
 22|
 23|「환대해 주셔서 감사합니다, 대통령님.」
 24|
 25|「한국에서 합동 국가장이 치러졌다는 것은 알고 있습니다. 불의에 의하여 안타깝게 희생된 피해자들. 그리고 전 평화 길드장이셨던 미스터 킴의 명복을 빕니다.」
 26|
 27|도람프 대통령은 외모뿐만 아니라 태도도 신사적이었다.
 28|
 29|합동 국가장에 주한미국대사와 외교부 장관을 보내어 도리를 지켰음에도, 이렇게 잊지 않고 따로 인사를 건네는 것만 봐도 알 수 있었다.
 30|
 31|「그러고 보니 외교부 장관과는 이미 구면이겠군요. 안 그래요, 제시?」
 32|
 33|도널드 대통령의 부름에 오각형 테이블에 앉아 있던 중년 여성, 외교부 장관이 빙긋 웃으며 눈인사를 건넨다.
 34|
 35|나는 그제야 이 자리에 있는 이들이 미합중국이라는 초강대국을 지탱하는 주축 인사들이라는 것을 깨달았다.
 36|
 37|‘미 군부와 정계의 핵심 인사들.’
 38|
 39|정장을 입은 이들은 몇 되지 않았다. 지난 합동 국가장 참석으로 일면식이 있는 외교부 장관이 그중 한 사람인 것으로 보아, 아마 정장을 입은 이들 대부분이 장관급이거나 그에 준하는 신분일 것이다.
 40|
 41|그리고 군부는…….
 42|
 43|‘더럽게 많네.’
 44|
 45|말 그대로 별들의 잔치다.
 46|
 47|반백이 되었거나 온통 흰머리로 가득한 중, 노년의 장군들이 정복(正服)에 반짝이는 휘장과 별을 단 채 호기심 어린 시선으로 이쪽을 바라보고 있었다.
 48|
 49|「아, 소개가 늦었군요.」
 50|
 51|내 시선이 향하는 방향을 알아차린 도람프 대통령이 말을 이었다.
 52|
 53|「자, 여러분. 이쪽은 평화 길드와 아레스 길드를 맡은 미스터 최. 또 모두가 아시는 미스터 진입니다. 그리고 이쪽에 계신 분들은…….」
 54|
 55|잭. 필립. 조이. 리암. 이사벨라.
 56|
 57|할리우드 전쟁 영화에서 한 번씩은 들어 본 이름과 직책이 휙휙 스쳐 지나간다.
 58|
 59|평소에도 모르는 게 없는 최 팀장은 그들의 얼굴과 이름을 다 알고 있는 것 같았지만, 나는 멍하니 고개만 끄덕였다.
 60|
 61|‘뭐 이렇게 부서나 직책들이 많아.’
 62|
 63|그나마 기억에 남는 인물들이 있었다면 CIA와 FBI의 국장 정도다. 아마 영화에서 자주 등장하던 특수 조직이라 그런 거겠지만.
 64|
 65|「소개도 끝났으니, 이제 두 분을 갑작스럽게 모신 이유에 대해 알려 드려야겠군요.」
 66|
 67|딱. 파앗!
 68|
 69|도람프 대통령이 경쾌하게 손가락을 튕긴 순간. 잠시 사라졌던 홀로그램이 사방을 가득 채웠다.
 70|
 71|‘이건.’
 72|
 73|지도다. 그것도 지구 전체가 아닌 특정 지역을 세밀하게 표현한 지도.
 74|
 75|수많은 건물과 각종 지형 위에는 좌표가 적혀 있었고, 곳곳에 별처럼 반짝이는 의미불명의 표시가 보였다.
 76|
 77|‘아.’
 78|
 79|홀로그램 지도에 적혀 있는 지명과 사막이 산재한 지형.
 80|
 81|그리고 막 도착했을 무렵 도람프 대통령이 하던 말을 떠올린 나는 깨달음과 함께 중얼거렸다.
 82|
 83|“중동?”
 84|
 85|「테러 단체의 위치를 표시한 전술 지도군요. 저 반짝거리는 표식은 게이트나 본거지일 테고.」
 86|
 87|입을 연 것은 나뿐만이 아니었다. 거의 동시에 흘러나온 나와 최 팀장의 말에, 도람프 대통령이 고개를 끄덕였다.
 88|
 89|「두 가지 모두 정답입니다. 다만 미스터 최의 대답이 훨씬 더 자세하고 정답에 가까웠어요. 저 빛은 테러 단체의 본거지로 추정되는 장소들을 표시해 놓은 겁니다. 홀로그램 축소.」
 90|
 91|슈우웅.
 92|
 93|명령어를 따라 커진 홀로그램이 지구본의 형상으로 줄어든다.
 94|
 95|도람프 대통령의 손짓에 따라 천천히 회전하는 지구 곳곳에 크고 작은 빛이 서려 있었다.
 96|
 97|“저게 다 테러 단체라고요?”
 98|
 99|「제 선친께서 대통령이던 시절에는 이슬람계 테러 조직의 숫자만 100개가 넘었습니다. 물론 대격변 이후에는 무서울 정도로 증식했고요.」
100|
101|이건 처음 알았네.
102|
103|이슬람계 테러 조직만 따져도 100개. 그것도 대격변 이전의 숫자이니 지금은 말할 것도 없다.
104|
105|물론 저 중에는 동아리 수준의 소규모 테러 집단도 있겠지만, 문제는 그놈들이 무슨 만화 동아리 활동이 아니라 살상을 목표로 한 테러 활동을 벌인다는 것이 문제다.
106|
107|‘아니, 뭐 이렇게 많아.’
108|
109|세상에 미친놈들이 많다는 것 정도는 알고 있었지만, 이 정도일 줄은 꿈에도 몰랐다.
110|
111|가라앉은 눈빛으로 홀로그램을 바라보던 최 팀장이 입을 열었다.
112|
113|「아프리카 곳곳에 산재한 반군 세력은 제외한 겁니까?」
114|
115|「좋은 질문입니다, 미스터 최. 하지만 다행히 반군 역시 포함되어 있는 숫자입니다.」
116|
117|「대통령님께서 말씀하신 것처럼 정말 천만다행이군요. 그리고 저희를 굳이 초청하신 이유 역시 알 것 같습니다.」
118|
119|최 팀장이 낮은 목소리로 말을 이었다.
120|
121|「아마도…… 테러 단체를 토벌할 생각이시겠죠.」
122|
123|「맞습니다.」
124|
125|도람프 대통령은 부정하지 않고 무겁게 고개를 끄덕였다.
126|
127|「두 분께서도 아시다시피, 미합중국은 여전히 세계 최강국이지만 그만큼의 견제를 받습니다. 그렇기에 군사적, 외교적으로 신중을 기할 수밖에 없지요.」
128|
129|미국이 아무리 유서 깊은 국제 깡패라고 해도 전 세계의 모든 나라를 씹어먹을 정도는 아니다.
130|
131|대격변을 겪으며 가장 극심한 피해를 입은 후에는 더더욱 그랬다.
132|
133|「하지만 현재 전 세계에서 암약하는 테러 단체와 반군은 하루빨리 사라져야 합니다. 그 이유에 관해서는 두 분 모두 잘 아실 테고요.」
134|
135|알다마다.
136|
137|매직 존슨도 언급했던 것처럼, 테러 단체와 아프리카 반군은 게이트와 마정석을 이용한 실험에 착수했다.
138|
139|그들이 실험을 통해서 어떤 결과를 얻을 것이며, 성공과 실패할지의 유무를 알 수는 없지만…… 확실한 건 그 자체만으로도 충분히 위험하다는 것이다.
140|
141|‘마치 핵실험처럼.’
142|
143|북한이 미사일 실험만 해도 전 세계의 시선이 주목된다.
144|
145|물론 한국인들이야 저 새끼들 또 지랄이네, 하면서 각자 할 일을 하지만 그건 결국 저놈들이 쏘지 않을 것이라는 걸 알기 때문이다.
146|
147|하지만 테러 집단은 북한처럼, 아니 그 이상으로 미친놈들이었다.
148|
149|「미스터 존슨에게 이야기를 들었을 겁니다. 당장 오늘만 해도 테러 집단은 캘리포니아와 애리조나, 텍사스. 이 세 곳에서 동시에 같은 짓을 벌었죠. 그리고 이건 미국에서만 벌어지는 일이 아닙니다.」
150|
151|스윽.
152|
153|도람프 대통령이 부드럽게 홀로그램 사이를 휘젓자, 지구본 형상이 사라지고 수십여 개에 달하는 작은 홀로그램 창들이 떠올랐다.
154|
155|- 투항하라! 지금이라도 무기를 버리고 투항한다면……!
156|
157|- 신은 위대하시다!
158|
159|- 피, 피해!
160|
161|- 콰아아앙!
162|
163|시스템을 통해 해석되는 수십 개의 언어가 시끄럽게 뒤섞였다.
164|
165|피부색과 생김새가 다른 그들은 폭발을 피해 도망치거나, 사방으로 튄 인간의 뼈와 살을 뒤집어쓴 채 비명을 지르고 있었다.
166|
167|「전 세계를 대상으로 오늘 하루만 32회의 테러 시도가 있었습니다. 다행히 뉴스에 보도된 텍사스 사태처럼 아직 피해는 미미하지만, 테러 집단이 소유하고 있는 게이트와 마정석을 이용해 실험을 끝마친다면…….」
168|
169|척 헤이글이 시가를 만지작거리며 거칠게 끼어들었다.
170|
171|「Fuck. 말할 것도 없이 다 좆 되는 거야. 이번 사우스 코리아에서 벌어진 사건처럼 몬스터 웨이브가 시도 때도 없이 일어나겠지.」
172|
173|매직 존슨 역시 한숨처럼 입을 열었다.
174|
175|「반군 역시 가만히 있지 않을 거고. 그놈들도 테러 집단만큼이나 위험해. 아이들까지 잡아다가 세뇌시키고 병사로 쓰는 놈들이니까. 나라를 차지하기 위해서라면 수만, 수십만이 죽어도 눈 하나 까딱하지 않을걸?”」
176|
177|이 세상에서 가장 선한 것도, 가장 악랄한 것도 인간이라는 말이 문득 생각나는 것은 왜일까.
178|
179|동시에 불과 몇 주 전 눈앞에서 죽어 간 이들의 시신과 비명이 다시 한번 떠올라 가슴 한구석을 무겁게 짓눌렀다.
180|
181|“음.”
182|
183|나는 침음성과 함께 최 팀장을 곁눈질했다.
184|
185|얼마 전 곁을 떠나간 누군가를 떠올리는 그의 시선은 깊게 가라앉아 있었다.
186|
187|‘두 번 다시 그런 일이 벌어져서는 안 돼.’
188|
189|모르겠다. 사람이 얼마나 악랄해질 수 있는지.
190|
191|몇이나 되는 사람들이 죽고 다쳐야 이 미친 쳇바퀴가 멈출지.
192|
193|하지만 동시에 다행이라는 생각이 들었다.
194|
195|내게는 끊임없이 돌아가는 이 쳇바퀴를 잠시나마 멈출 만한 힘이 있으니까.
196|
197|설령 멈출 수 없다면…….
198|
199|‘부숴 버려야지.’
200|
201|마음속에서 이미 결정을 끝낸 나는 도람프 대통령을 응시하며 불쑥 입을 열었다.
202|
203|“토벌 작전은 언제쯤 시작합니까?”
204|
205|내 물음에 담긴 뜻을 알아차린 그의 입가에 미소가 번진다.
206|
207|도람프 대통령의 눈짓에 오각형 테이블에 앉아 있던 이들 중 한 사람이 일어났다.
208|
209|「UN 상임 이사회 전부가 동의한다는 전제하에, 모든 준비가 끝나기까지 빠르면 두 달. 길면 반년 이상으로 예상됩니다.」
210|
211|“빠르면 두 달?”
212|
213|느리다. 생각했던 것보다도 훨씬.
214|
215|나는 작게 눈살을 찌푸리며 말을 이었다.
216|
217|“위험성을 말씀하신 것치고는 너무 시간이 지체되는 것 같은데요.”
218|
219|「국제법상 어쩔 수 없습니다. 특히 중동과 아프리카 지역에 자국 동의 없이 병력을 투입하는 건 명백한 주권 침해입니다.」
220|
221|“현대 역사 교과서 보니까 중동 지역에서는 잘만 싸웠던데, 뭘. 예전에 오일머니 관련 비판 다큐도 봤어요.”
222|
223|별생각 없이 툭 던진 내 말에 순간 말문이 막힌 정부 핵심 인사가 헛기침을 내뱉었다.
224|
225|「……크흠. 그건 911사태 때문이었고, 지금은 대격변 이후 새로 맺은 국제 협약에 따라.」
226|
227|“그럼 됐고. 어쨌든 정말 빨라야 두 달 정도라는 거죠?”
228|
229|「크흐흠. 예. 그렇습니다.」
230|

Sure, some were probably little groups that operated on the scale of clubs. The problem was, they weren’t meeting to talk about comics. They carried out attacks to kill people.

[P51]
*Seriously, why are there so many?*

[P52]
I knew the world had plenty of lunatics. I’d never imagined there were this many.

[P53]
Team Leader Choi watched the hologram, his gaze dark.

[P54]
“Does that exclude the rebel forces scattered across Africa?”

[P55]
“A good question, Mr. Choi. Fortunately, the rebels are included.”

[P56]
“As you say, Mr. President, that’s fortunate indeed. And I think I understand why you invited us.”

[P57]
His voice dropped.

[P58]
“You’re planning to take down the terrorist groups.”

[P59]
“That’s right.”

[P60]
President Doramp gave a grave nod.

[P61]
“As you both know, the United States remains the strongest nation in the world. That also means our actions face scrutiny. We have no choice but to proceed carefully, both militarily and diplomatically.”

[P62]
The United States might have a long history as the world’s bully, but even it couldn’t push around every country on Earth. That was especially true after it had suffered the worst losses in the Great Cataclysm.

[P63]
“But the terrorist groups and rebels operating around the world must be eliminated as soon as possible. I’m sure you both know why.”

[P64]
Of course I did.

[P65]
As Magic Johnson had told us, the terrorist groups and African rebels had begun experimenting with Gates and Magic Gems.

[P66]
I didn’t know what those experiments would produce, or whether they would succeed. But the experiments alone were dangerous enough.

[P67]
*Like nuclear tests.*

[P68]
The whole world paid attention whenever North Korea tested a missile.

[P69]
Koreans, of course, just thought, *Those bastards are at it again,* and got on with their day. But that was because we knew they weren’t going to fire at us.

[P70]
Terrorist groups were as crazy as North Korea. Crazier, even.

[P71]
“You must have heard from Mr. Johnson. Today alone, terrorist groups carried out the same kind of attack simultaneously in California, Arizona, and Texas. And this isn’t happening only in the United States.”

[P72]
President Doramp swept a hand through the hologram.

[P73]
The globe vanished. Dozens of small windows took its place.

[P74]
> “Surrender! Put down your weapons now, and…!”
>
> “God is great!”
>
> “R-run!”
>
> “BOOM!”

[P75]
Dozens of languages, translated for me by the System, mingled in a deafening clamor.

[P76]
People of different appearances and skin colors fled explosions or screamed as human bone and flesh sprayed over them.

[P77]
“There have been thirty-two attempted attacks around the world today alone. Fortunately, as with the incident in Texas that made the news, the damage so far has been minor. But if the terrorist groups complete their experiments with the Gates and Magic Gems in their possession…”

[P78]
Chuck Hagel, fiddling with his cigar, cut in.

[P79]
“Fuck. Everything goes to shit. Monster waves will break out at any time, anywhere, just like what happened in South Korea.”

[P80]
Magic Johnson spoke with a sigh.

[P81]
“And the rebels won’t sit still, either. They’re every bit as dangerous. They kidnap children, brainwash them, and use them as soldiers. They wouldn’t bat an eye if tens or hundreds of thousands died so they could take over a country.”

[P82]
Why did that remind me of the saying that human beings were capable of both the greatest good and the greatest evil?

[P83]
The bodies of the people who had died before my eyes only weeks ago came back to me. So did their screams. A weight settled in my chest.

[P84]
“Hmm.”

[P85]
I glanced at Team Leader Choi. His gaze had gone distant, as though he, too, was thinking of someone he’d lost recently.

[P86]
*That can’t happen again.*

[P87]
I didn’t know how cruel people could become, or how many had to die or be hurt before this insane wheel stopped turning.

[P88]
But one thought gave me hope: I had the power to stop it, if only for a little while.

[P89]
And if I couldn’t stop it…

[P90]
*I’ll break it.*

[P91]
My mind made up, I looked straight at President Doramp.

[P92]
“When does the operation begin?”

[P93]
He understood what I meant. A smile spread across his face, and at his signal, someone at the pentagonal table stood.

[P94]
“Assuming every permanent member of the UN Security Council agrees, it will take at least two months to complete preparations. It could take more than six.”

[P95]
“Two months at the earliest?”

[P96]
Slow. Far slower than I’d expected.

[P97]
I frowned.

[P98]
“After everything you’ve said about the danger, that seems like a long time.”

[P99]
“International law leaves us little choice. Deploying troops to countries in the Middle East and Africa without their consent would be a clear violation of their sovereignty.”

[P100]
“Funny. My modern history textbooks made it look like you fought in the Middle East just fine. I watched a documentary criticizing the oil money involved, too.”

[P101]
I’d tossed that out without much thought. The senior official who’d been answering me fell silent, then cleared his throat.

[P102]
“Ahem… That was because of the 9/11 attacks. Under the new international agreements made after the Great Cataclysm—”

[P103]
“Never mind. Two months really is the absolute earliest?”

[P104]
“Ahem. Yes.”

[P105]
I thought for a moment, then leaned close to President Doramp and whispered.

[P106]
“Can I ask you something?”

[P107]
“Anything.”

[P108]
“Suppose someone nobody could identify—some mysterious stranger, for example—wiped out the African rebels or the terrorist groups in the Middle East. Would *that* break international law?”

[P109]
“Pardon?”

[P110]
“Batman. Spider-Man. Someone like that. And lower your voice before you answer.”

[P111]
President Doramp stared blankly at me. When he finally caught on, he struggled to get the words out.

[P112]
“You mean to say you intend to hide your identity and take down the terrorist groups…?”

[P113]
“Me? Why would I?”

[P114]
“But what you just said—”

[P115]
“I never said that. It was an example.”

[P116]
“W-wait, Mr. Jin.”

[P117]
“You’re going to get someone in trouble, mister. Why would I do a thing like that alone? You’d have to be some lunatic who’d storm Ares Guild headquarters by himself.”

[P118]
“…!”

[P119]
A suffocating silence filled the room.

[P120]
President Doramp stared at me as if I were insane. At last, he spoke.

[P121]
“It seems I misunderstood. What an absurd thought.”

[P122]
“Right?”

[P123]
“Yes. In that case, we’ll end today’s meeting here. I’m going to leave the holographic tactical map behind by accident.”

[P124]
“Ah. An accident.”

[P125]
“Yes. It’s classified at the highest level, so it must never leave this room. Especially since it shows the precise locations of rebel forces in the Middle East and Africa.”

[P126]
“Anything else?”

[P127]
“Everything necessary is in the materials. Not that you’ll have any opportunity to obtain them, Mr. Jin. You’ll be heading straight back to Korea, won’t you, Mr. Johnson?”

[P128]
Magic Johnson had caught on. He nodded.

[P129]
“Of course, Mr. President. Though Jin likes to travel. I wonder if it would be all right for me to take a few days off and spend some time with him.”

[P130]
“Is that so? Is there anywhere you particularly like to—”

[P131]
“Africa and the Middle East,” I said without drawing breath. “I go crazy for deserts. My dream is to pee in an oasis and give the Sphinx some Churu[^1].”

[P132]
Team Leader Choi added calmly, “I was born in summer, so I like hot places.”

[P133]
“Well. What a coincidence.”

[P134]
“Ready, Choi?”

[P135]
“Of course, Johnson… No, that sounds a little strange.”

[P136]
The conversation was bewildering, yet somehow going remarkably smoothly. Chuck Hagel clamped his cigar between his teeth and put an end to it.

[P137]
“A lunatic going to kill lunatics.”

[P138]
He was right. Lunatics ought to die at the hands of a lunatic.

[P139]
* * *

[P140]
It was an ordinary day.

[P141]
Muhammad Saladir ad-Din, leader of an armed Islamic terrorist group, had interrogated a foreign prisoner and killed a subordinate who’d gotten mouthy. Then he returned to his bedroom.

[P142]
Before he could take off his outer clothes, he found an uninvited guest waiting for him.

[P143]
“Stand up straight, Hassan.”

[P144]
“…?”

[P145]
[^1]: Churu is a popular lickable cat treat.

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.

He had already done the proper thing by sending the U.S. ambassador to Korea and the Secretary of State to the funeral. Yet he had remembered to offer his condolences in person, too.

[P15]
“Come to think of it, you’ve already met the Secretary of State, haven’t you? Isn’t that right, Jesse?”

[P16]
At his call, the middle-aged woman seated at the pentagonal table smiled and greeted us with a glance.

[P17]
Only then did it hit me: the people in this room were the ones holding up the superpower that was the United States.

[P18]
*The top brass of the U.S. military and government.*

[P19]
Only a few wore suits. The Secretary of State, whom I’d met briefly at the funeral, was among them. The others were probably cabinet members or held positions just as high.

[P20]
As for the military…

[P21]
*There are a shitload of them.*

[P22]
It was a feast of stars, literally.

[P23]
Middle-aged and elderly generals, their hair either going gray or already white, watched us with curiosity. Insignia and stars gleamed on their dress uniforms.

[P24]
“Ah, I should introduce everyone.”

[P25]
President Doramp noticed where I was looking.

[P26]
“Everyone, this is Mr. Choi, who leads the Peace Guild and Ares Guild. And this is Mr. Jin, whom you all know. As for the people here…”

[P27]
Jack. Philip. Joey. Liam. Isabella.

[P28]
Names and titles I’d heard in Hollywood war movies flew past me.

[P29]
Team Leader Choi seemed to know every face and name, as usual. I just stared and nodded.

[P30]
*How many departments and titles are there?*

[P31]
The only people who stuck in my mind were the directors of the CIA and FBI. Probably because those organizations showed up in movies so often.

[P32]
“Now that we’ve made the introductions, I should tell you why we brought you here so suddenly.”

[P33]
Snap. Fwoosh!

[P34]
President Doramp snapped his fingers, and the hologram that had vanished when we arrived filled the room again.

[P35]
*This is…*

[P36]
A map. Not of the whole Earth, but a detailed map of one region.

[P37]
Coordinates hovered over countless buildings and stretches of terrain. Markers whose meaning I couldn’t guess glittered here and there like stars.

[P38]
*Oh.*

[P39]
The place names. The deserts scattered across the map. And what President Doramp had been saying when we arrived.

[P40]
I put it together and muttered, “The Middle East?”

[P41]
“It’s a tactical map showing terrorist-group locations. Those markers must be Gates or bases.”

[P42]
Team Leader Choi had spoken almost at the same time as me. President Doramp nodded to us both.

[P43]
“You’re both right, though Mr. Choi’s answer is more detailed and closer to the mark. The lights indicate suspected terrorist bases. Hologram, zoom out.”

[P44]
Whoosh.

[P45]
The enlarged map shrank into a globe. It turned slowly at President Doramp’s gesture, lights large and small scattered across its surface.

[P46]
“All of those are terrorist groups?”

[P47]
“When my late father was president, there were already more than a hundred Islamic terrorist organizations alone. After the Great Cataclysm, of course, they multiplied at a frightening rate.”

[P48]
That was news to me.

[P49]
More than a hundred Islamic terrorist organizations *before* the Great Cataclysm. Who knew how many there were now?

[P50]
Sure, some were probably little groups that operated on the scale of clubs. The problem was, they weren’t meeting to talk about comics. They carried out attacks to kill people.

[P51]
*Seriously, why are there so many?*

[P52]
I knew the world had plenty of lunatics. I’d never imagined there were this many.

[P53]
Team Leader Choi watched the hologram, his gaze dark.

[P54]
“Does that exclude the rebel forces scattered across Africa?”

[P55]
“A good question, Mr. Choi. Fortunately, the rebels are included.”

[P56]
“As you say, Mr. President, that’s fortunate indeed. And I think I understand why you invited us.”

[P57]
His voice dropped.

[P58]
“You’re planning to take down the terrorist groups.”

[P59]
“That’s right.”

[P60]
President Doramp gave a grave nod.

[P61]
“As you both know, the United States remains the strongest nation in the world. That also means our actions face scrutiny. We have no choice but to proceed carefully, both militarily and diplomatically.”

[P62]
The United States might have a long history as the world’s bully, but even it couldn’t push around every country on Earth. That was especially true after it had suffered the worst losses in the Great Cataclysm.

[P63]
“But the terrorist groups and rebels operating around the world must be eliminated as soon as possible. I’m sure you both know why.”

[P64]
Of course I did.

[P65]
As Magic Johnson had told us, the terrorist groups and African rebels had begun experimenting with Gates and Magic Gems.

[P66]
I didn’t know what those experiments would produce, or whether they would succeed. But the experiments alone were dangerous enough.

[P67]
*Like nuclear tests.*

[P68]
The whole world paid attention whenever North Korea tested a missile.

[P69]
Koreans, of course, just thought, *Those bastards are at it again,* and got on with their day. But that was because we knew they weren’t going to fire at us.

[P70]
Terrorist groups were as crazy as North Korea. Crazier, even.

[P71]
“You must have heard from Mr. Johnson. Today alone, terrorist groups carried out the same kind of attack simultaneously in California, Arizona, and Texas. And this isn’t happening only in the United States.”

[P72]
President Doramp swept a hand through the hologram.

[P73]
The globe vanished. Dozens of small windows took its place.

[P74]
> “Surrender! Put down your weapons now, and…!”
>
> “God is great!”
>
> “R-run!”
>
> “BOOM!”

[P75]
Dozens of languages, translated for me by the System, mingled in a deafening clamor.

[P76]
People of different appearances and skin colors fled explosions or screamed as human bone and flesh sprayed over them.

[P77]
“There have been thirty-two attempted attacks around the world today alone. Fortunately, as with the incident in Texas that made the news, the damage so far has been minor. But if the terrorist groups complete their experiments with the Gates and Magic Gems in their possession…”

[P78]
Chuck Hagel, fiddling with his cigar, cut in.

[P79]
“Fuck. Everything goes to shit. Monster waves will break out at any time, anywhere, just like what happened in South Korea.”

[P80]
Magic Johnson spoke with a sigh.

[P81]
“And the rebels won’t sit still, either. They’re every bit as dangerous. They kidnap children, brainwash them, and use them as soldiers. They wouldn’t bat an eye if tens or hundreds of thousands died so they could take over a country.”

[P82]
Why did that remind me of the saying that human beings were capable of both the greatest good and the greatest evil?

[P83]
The bodies of the people who had died before my eyes only weeks ago came back to me. So did their screams. A weight settled in my chest.

[P84]
“Hmm.”

[P85]
I glanced at Team Leader Choi. His gaze had gone distant, as though he, too, was thinking of someone he’d lost recently.

[P86]
*That can’t happen again.*

[P87]
I didn’t know how cruel people could become, or how many had to die or be hurt before this insane wheel stopped turning.

[P88]
But one thought gave me hope: I had the power to stop it, if only for a little while.

[P89]
And if I couldn’t stop it…

[P90]
*I’ll break it.*

[P91]
My mind made up, I looked straight at President Doramp.

[P92]
“When does the operation begin?”

[P93]
He understood what I meant. A smile spread across his face, and at his signal, someone at the pentagonal table stood.

[P94]
“Assuming every permanent member of the UN Security Council agrees, it will take at least two months to complete preparations. It could take more than six.”

[P95]
“Two months at the earliest?”

[P96]
Slow. Far slower than I’d expected.

[P97]
I frowned.

[P98]
“After everything you’ve said about the danger, that seems like a long time.”

[P99]
“International law leaves us little choice. Deploying troops to countries in the Middle East and Africa without their consent would be a clear violation of their sovereignty.”

[P100]
“Funny. My modern history textbooks made it look like you fought in the Middle East just fine. I watched a documentary criticizing the oil money involved, too.”

[P101]
I’d tossed that out without much thought. The senior official who’d been answering me fell silent, then cleared his throat.

[P102]
“Ahem… That was because of the 9/11 attacks. Under the new international agreements made after the Great Cataclysm—”

[P103]
“Never mind. Two months really is the absolute earliest?”

[P104]
“Ahem. Yes.”

[P105]
I thought for a moment, then leaned close to President Doramp and whispered.

[P106]
“Can I ask you something?”

[P107]
“Anything.”

[P108]
“Suppose someone nobody could identify—some mysterious stranger, for example—wiped out the African rebels or the terrorist groups in the Middle East. Would *that* break international law?”

[P109]
“Pardon?”

[P110]
“Batman. Spider-Man. Someone like that. And lower your voice before you answer.”

[P111]
President Doramp stared blankly at me. When he finally caught on, he struggled to get the words out.

[P112]
“You mean to say you intend to hide your identity and take down the terrorist groups…?”

[P113]
“Me? Why would I?”

[P114]
“But what you just said—”

[P115]
“I never said that. It was an example.”

[P116]
“W-wait, Mr. Jin.”

[P117]
“You’re going to get someone in trouble, mister. Why would I do a thing like that alone? You’d have to be some lunatic who’d storm Ares Guild headquarters by himself.”

[P118]
“…!”

[P119]
A suffocating silence filled the room.

[P120]
President Doramp stared at me as if I were insane. At last, he spoke.

[P121]
“It seems I misunderstood. What an absurd thought.”

[P122]
“Right?”

[P123]
“Yes. In that case, we’ll end today’s meeting here. I’m going to leave the holographic tactical map behind by accident.”

[P124]
“Ah. An accident.”

[P125]
“Yes. It’s classified at the highest level, so it must never leave this room. Especially since it shows the precise locations of rebel forces in the Middle East and Africa.”

[P126]
“Anything else?”

[P127]
“Everything necessary is in the materials. Not that you’ll have any opportunity to obtain them, Mr. Jin. You’ll be heading straight back to Korea, won’t you, Mr. Johnson?”

[P128]
Magic Johnson had caught on. He nodded.

[P129]
“Of course, Mr. President. Though Jin likes to travel. I wonder if it would be all right for me to take a few days off and spend some time with him.”

[P130]
“Is that so? Is there anywhere you particularly like to—”

[P131]
“Africa and the Middle East,” I said without drawing breath. “I go crazy for deserts. My dream is to pee in an oasis and give the Sphinx some Churu[^1].”

[P132]
Team Leader Choi added calmly, “I was born in summer, so I like hot places.”

[P133]
“Well. What a coincidence.”

[P134]
“Ready, Choi?”

[P135]
“Of course, Johnson… No, that sounds a little strange.”

[P136]
The conversation was bewildering, yet somehow going remarkably smoothly. Chuck Hagel clamped his cigar between his teeth and put an end to it.

[P137]
“A lunatic going to kill lunatics.”

[P138]
He was right. Lunatics ought to die at the hands of a lunatic.

[P139]
* * *

[P140]
It was an ordinary day.

[P141]
Muhammad Saladir ad-Din, leader of an armed Islamic terrorist group, had interrogated a foreign prisoner and killed a subordinate who’d gotten mouthy. Then he returned to his bedroom.

[P142]
Before he could take off his outer clothes, he found an uninvited guest waiting for him.

[P143]
“Stand up straight, Hassan.”

[P144]
“…?”

[P145]
[^1]: Churu is a popular lickable cat treat.
```

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.

- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.

- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.

Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.
